name:        Switch
domain:      component
package:     @astryxdesign/core
import:      @astryxdesign/core/Switch
description: A toggle control for on/off states that take effect immediately. Supports labels, descriptions, loading states, and validation. Use it for settings or preferences that apply instantly. For changes requiring a form submission, use a checkbox instead. Under a finger it moves like the iOS switch on every touch screen: a press lifts the thumb, a drag across flips it, lifting the finger commits, and a tap toggles through the browser's click. The thumb keeps its circle and size on every device, and under a coarse pointer the invisible hit area grows toward 44 × 44 px, stopping halfway to any neighbouring control so a tap goes to the nearer one. With reduced motion on, a change cross-fades on a touch screen and is immediate with a mouse.
command:     npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 component Switch

name:        createReorderable
domain:      hook
package:     @astryxdesign/core
import:      @astryxdesign/core
description: Makes a collection's rows reorderable. On a touch screen a finger held still on a row's handle for a moment picks it up (a flick on the handle still scrolls): the row stays in its place, dimmed, while a copy of it follows the finger and an accent line marks where it would land; the other rows stay still, the page scrolls near its edges, and on release the rows rearrange. A pen held still on a handle where the primary pointer is coarse picks the row up as a finger does. A mouse, or a pen where the primary pointer is fine, drags a handle at once the same way, and the rows take their places without motion; a cancelled drag puts everything back at once. Without a drag, the handle toggles reorder mode for its row (a click, Space or Enter): each arrow key moves the row a place at once, and Escape or another activation ends the mode, keeping the moves; screen readers hear each move with the row's place and neighbours, and a hint shows the moves and Done as buttons, for taps alone. The reorder code ships with this function: a collection without the prop loads none of it.
command:     npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 hook createReorderable

name:        useAnnounce
domain:      hook
package:     @astryxdesign/core
import:      @astryxdesign/core/hooks
description: Imperatively announces a message to screen readers through a visually-hidden live region. Use it for state that is only conveyed visually; search result counts, "no results", loading and saved confirmations, validation errors (WCAG 4.1.3 Status Messages). The polite and assertive regions are created empty on first use and stay mounted, which is what makes announcements reliable: most screen readers ignore a live region that is inserted together with its content. Each message is cleared a couple of seconds after it is announced so stale status does not linger in the accessibility tree. A message is delivered where its caller is: from inside an open Astryx modal it goes to a region inside that modal and is heard there with no change to the calling code; a message sent just as the modal is dismissed is delivered through whatever is exposed afterwards rather than lost. A call made outside the modal, even by the component that renders it, uses the page-body region.
command:     npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 hook useAnnounce

name:        useEntryAnimation
domain:      hook
package:     @astryxdesign/core
import:      @astryxdesign/core/hooks
description: Returns a StyleX style for animating an element on mount. Only animates when the element is dynamically inserted after the initial page paint; elements rendered on page load are not animated. Uses Astryx motion tokens (duration, easing) for consistent animation timing. Server-rendered elements hydrate without the entry style and never animate; elements mounted after hydration animate.
command:     npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 hook useEntryAnimation

name:        useImageMode
domain:      hook
package:     @astryxdesign/core
import:      @astryxdesign/core/hooks
description: Detects whether an image is predominantly dark or light by sampling pixels via OffscreenCanvas. Uses APCA perceptual lightness (sRGB linearization + power curve) for accurate detection, especially on saturated colors. Runs entirely off the paint path: no visible canvas, no layout thrash. Supports regional sampling for detecting luminance where text overlays will appear. Returns null while loading and falls back gracefully on CORS or network errors.
command:     npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 hook useImageMode

name:        useSnapPaging
domain:      hook
package:     @astryxdesign/core
import:      @astryxdesign/core/SnapPaging
description: Gives a Carousel iOS paging on native snap's stops: pass the value as hasSnap={useSnapPaging()}. Under a finger and on a trackpad swipe, a flick moves one view, or one item with {pages: 'item'}, and the row rests on an item's start edge. A mouse wheel keeps native snapping. Only a carousel given the value loads the paging code.
command:     npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 hook useSnapPaging

name:        useTableGroupedRows
domain:      hook
package:     @astryxdesign/core
import:      @astryxdesign/core/hooks
description: Hook that groups a flat data array into collapsible section rows. Each distinct groupBy value becomes a full-width section-header row with a chevron toggle, the group label, and a member count; collapsing hides that group's data rows while keeping the header visible. The disclosure state lives on the chevron button, not the native table row. Mirrors useTableTreeState: the consumer owns the collapsedGroups set and the hook returns {data, plugin, idKey}: pass them to Table as data, plugins, and idKey respectively. Grouping runs on the rows you hand it, so with pagination the order is filter, sort, slice, then group: sort by the group key first and the user's keys second, so a section's rows stay contiguous and each page appends to the bottom of the table instead of splicing rows in above the reader. A page that ends on a row count still cuts mid-section, and the heading then counts what has loaded rather than what exists: "6" quietly becoming "10". Where the full result set is in hand, carry the cut forward to the end of the section it lands in: every rendered section is then whole and its count is a total.
command:     npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 hook useTableGroupedRows
